title: Setup-script exit 2 ('[x]abort', documented as stop the run) is treated as an ordinary failure: both installers continue with the next step and scripts/aitools reports 'Completed with errors'
observation: interactive-menus.md:74 and :88 say only `abort` is global ('stop the run'); aitools-lib.sh:915 and :1075 ('Exits with code 2 on abort'); reference/managed-file-deployment.md:44 and :54 ('[x]abort --> exit 2'). aitools-install.sh validate_and_run (:154-173) logs any non-zero exit as '<name> failed (exit N)' with write_summary ERROR and returns, and the installer goes on to the next step (call sites such as :291, :609, :721); aitools-install.ps1 Invoke-ValidatedScript (:92-119) does the same. scripts/aitools:1604-1616 maps any installer non-zero to 'Completed with errors' and overall_rc=1; aitools.ps1:1495-1509 does the same ($installerRc non-zero -> 'Completed with errors', $overallRc = 1).
expected: .claude/rules/interactive-menus.md 'JSON field-level review' (abort is global, stops the run); reference/managed-file-deployment.md state machine ([x]abort --> exit 2).
impact: A user who chooses [x]abort in a managed-file or JSON field review still gets every later installer step run against their machine, and the run is reported as an error rather than an abort.
discoveryContext: Found by mission S5-Tools (I-02, I-24; reviewer S5-Tools-A D-07) (session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-20/21) and consolidated by S4-Review, which de-duplicated it against incidents #1-#86 (origin/main 26c37b2 registries/incidents.json). Audited: interactive-menus.md, aitools-lib.sh prompt_diff_review, aitools-install.sh validate_and_run, aitools-install.ps1 Invoke-ValidatedScript, scripts/aitools installer_rc handling. Citations re-verified by S3-Ledger (mission LEDGER, session 10cf255a-c) against origin/main c8573ed on 2026-10-21; file:line references added.
suggestedResolution: Installer contract (reference/tool-support-decision-tree.md draft 7.5): exit 2 = user abort; runners write no failure row, stop remaining steps, render the summary, exit 2; entry points propagate 2 and print 'aborted by user'. Bash and PS1 together.

title: No framework or rule governs artifact placement (user level, project level or source), so placement follows an unwritten folder convention
observation: registries/framework-registry.json lists 13 frameworks (Three-layer governance, Incident governance, Source-of-truth protection, Tool lifecycle, Managed file deployment, Hook rollout, Incident investigation, Framework adoption, Governed vocabulary, Intent documentation, Governed data access, Artifact harvesting, Tool operations); none governs where an artifact is authored or which level it deploys to. .claude/rules/documentation-standards.md 'Skill placement' covers skills only. S2-Layout report section 2: the CLAUDE.md text that explained the split was deleted in b504c43, and registries/ and reference/ carry no level. Instances: #113 (same-name skills), #123 (trigger rules at the wrong level), #59 and #70 (user-level skills and hooks reading repo-relative registry paths).
expected: No spec exists for: artifact placement across levels. .claude/rules/frameworks.md 'Governing principle': at a decision point without guidance, check whether a framework addresses it.
impact: Each new skill, rule, hook or registry is placed by guess, and mistakes surface months later as shadowing, dead paths or triggers that never load (the instances above).
discoveryContext: Found by mission S2-Layout (report section 7, finding 12; /frameworks coverage check; session 360aa8f3-8, 2026-10-21). Re-verified and drafted by S3-Ledger (mission LEDGER, session 10cf255a-c) on origin/main c8573ed, 2026-10-21. frameworks: Configuration identification (ISO 10007, IEEE 828): every configuration item has a defined location and owner; folder-encodes-scope conventions such as the XDG Base Directory specification.
suggestedResolution: Adopt S2-Layout section 3 'folder = level' (shared/** = user, .claude/** and .cursor/** = project, everything else = source) as a 'Placement' section of the Managed file deployment framework (S2-Layout PR-b batch 6, via /frameworks; protected) plus the three-line rule in documentation-standards.md; the N2 check (#113) is its detection layer. Alternative: a separate 'Artifact placement' framework entry.
